notes: Hoffman 1862 (1846 / Pio Pico / R. S. Den / confirmed) agrees with both the register and the case file on year, governor and grantee. The underlying title instrument itself (Exhibit 'A' annexed to J. J. Warner's deposition, and Exhibit 'B No. 1 G.T.B.' annexed to Agustin Olvera's) was NOT found transcribed in the pages read; if it is transcribed it most likely sits at stamped pp. 40-58 (images 43-61), which I did not open. What I graded year/governor/grantee against is therefore the Land Commission's own opinion and decree, not the concession instrument - a decree, not testimony and not the petition, but one step removed from the grant. The exhibits that DO appear transcribed at stamped pp.61-65 (images 64-68) are context documents from Case No. 295, not this grant: a Ministry of Justice communication, Mexico 14 Nov. 1845, ordering all mission alienations suspended, and Tornel's Ministry of War order, Mexico 10 March 1846, empowering the Governor to raise funds for defence. Those two are the documents the U.S. was litigating against. IMAGE/STAMP OFFSET for this file: stamped page = image number - 3, stable from img 5 through img 75.

notes: Cleanest record of the six. The concession is here three times over: the archive expediente in Spanish (stamped pp.11-12, imgs 17-18, certified by Surveyor General Samuel D. King 24 Dec. 1852 as a true copy of archive document '1845 No. 21. Espediente sobre venta de misiones'); the claimant's own title copy in Spanish (stamped pp.17-18, imgs 23-24, Doc. H.H. No.1 annexed to Jose Abrego's deposition); and two independent English translations (Exhibit B by W. E. P. Hartnell, State Translator, Monterey 4 Oct. 1852, stamped pp.13-15, imgs 19-21; and a second at stamped pp.19-20, imgs 25-26). All four texts give 4 January 1846, Pio Pico, Feliciano Soberanes. Consideration was not cash but the extinguishment of a public debt of 'ochocientos y mas pesos' owed Soberanes for supplies furnished to Micheltorena's and Castro's divisions, under the Departmental Assembly's decree of 4 July 1845. Note the register's patent_acres 8,899.82 against the grant's 'dos sitios de ganado mayor' / 'two square leagues' (~8,877 acres) - a survey-sized difference, not a discrepancy I can call an error, and patent fields belong to Phase C anyway. Hoffman 1862 agrees on all four fields and on commission no. 526. IMAGE/STAMP OFFSET: stamped page = image number - 5, from img 7 onward (img 5 = stamped p.1, img 6 blank verso).

notes: Fully documented from the concession itself, not from testimony or the petition. The grant is an ENLARGEMENT: condition 1 of the decree (stamped p.10, img 16) states the land is conceded 'en ampliacion del terreno que poseen llamado Lompoc' - added to the Carrillos' existing Lompoc rancho. Consideration was paid in kind to the mission, not to the government: 25 heifers, 25 steers, 10 cows and 5 horses receipted by Fr. Juan Moreno, in charge of La Purisima, 20 June 1844 (Spanish at stamped p.8, img 14; translation stamped pp.16-17, imgs 22-23). Chronology worth preserving: title issued 20 Nov. 1845; expediente laid before the Departmental Assembly 8 May 1846; Committee on Vacant Lands reported 22 May 1846 (S. Arguello); Assembly approved 3 June 1846 (Pio Pico, President; Agustin Olvera, Deputy Secretary). The register's 1845 is the TITLE date, which is the right choice; a register that had used the Assembly-approval date would read 1846, and the petition at stamped p.4 (img 9) cites both. Both Spanish copies and both English translations agree on 20 Nov. 1845 - no translation/original date conflict here. Extent 'un sitio de ganado mayor' = one square league, against the register's patent_acres 4,413.60 (a league is 4,438.68 acres) - survey-sized difference, Phase C. Hoffman 1862 gives year 1845 and leaves governor and grantee blank, so the register is strictly RICHER than Hoffman here and both its added values check out against the decree. IMAGE/STAMP OFFSET is NOT constant in this file: img 5 = stamped p.1, then imgs 7-11 = pp.2-6, img 12 is an UNSTAMPED blank, img 13 = p.7, imgs 14-19 = pp.8-13, img 20 = p.14, img 21 = p.15, img 22 unstamped blank, imgs 23-24 = pp.16-17 ... verify the stamp on each leaf rather than assuming an offset.

notes: TRANSPORT FAILURE, not a source failure. From about 16:26 UTC 2026-09-09 digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu answers every scripted client with HTTP 202 and x-amzn-waf-action: challenge (an AWS WAF JavaScript challenge). curl and scripts/fetch_case_pages.py therefore receive zero bytes; note the status is 202, NOT an error code, so a naive caller sees 'success' and an empty file. I got one file (SD 061) by harvesting the aws-waf-token from a real Chrome session and replaying it in curl, but the token expires in minutes and the browser extension then refused to return it again (blocked as a sensitive key). Chrome-side downloads worked exactly once and were afterwards blocked as repeated automatic downloads; pushing the bytes out of the page to a localhost receiver is blocked by the site's connect-src CSP; the site's own PDF.js viewer would not instantiate; and there is no IIIF manifest and no Internet Archive copy. Re-run this record when the WAF relaxes, or drive the download from a browser session a human has just used. LEADS FOR THE RE-READER, all SECONDARY and none of them graded: the digicoll record page for this item carries J. N. Bowman's Index entry verbatim - 'Granted (1) by Alvarado Feb. 16, 1841, to Jose Antonio Estudillo provisionally, and (2) by Pico Apl. 4, 1845, to Augustin Olvera; about 16 leagues, by name. Claim filed by Juan Forster Oct. 16, 1852. Confirmed by the Board Oct. 31, 1854. Confirmed by the District Court Feb. 23, 1857; appeal dismissed June 4, 1857. Patent issued to Juan Forster Aug. 6, 1866, for 46,432.65 acres... In spite of this name this was not a part of the mission lands. Originally the grant was to Jose A. Estudillo Feb. 16, 1841; he abandoned the land and it was renounced June 8, 1843.' If that is right the register's 1845 / Pico / Agustin Olvera is the SECOND grant and is the correct choice, and the register has correctly kept the Mexican grantee (Olvera) in grantee and the U.S. claimant/patentee (Juan Forster) in patent_to - i.e. the dominant error class is absent. But note this file has TWO grants by two different governors eleven years apart, so it is exactly the kind of record where a reader who opens the wrong decree records 1841/Alvarado/Estudillo. Whoever re-reads must find the 4 April 1845 title and quote it.

notes: NULL READ, RECORDED AS A FINDING so the queue does not reissue it blindly. Unlike my other two ungraded records this is NOT the WAF problem: this item genuinely has no case-file PDF to download. The register's scan_record_url (record/102020) resolves and renders fine, but the rendered page contains ZERO '/files/' links and no Download control, and the derived name cubanc_lcf_sd390.pdf answers HTTP 200 with an HTML body rather than a PDF - precisely the documented trap where a wrong or absent filename returns 200 + HTML instead of 404, so a caller that trusts the status code will write a garbage 'PDF'. Contrast the two cubanc_lcf files I probed the same way in the same call, which correctly returned 206 + application/pdf + a content-range. LEADS FOR THE RE-READER, all SECONDARY and none of them graded: the digicoll record page carries Bowman's entry - 'Granted by Figueroa Aug. 1, 1834, to Candelario Valencia; 3 quarters of a leagues, by name. Claim filled by Elam Brown Feb. 2, 1852. Confirmed by the Board Feb. 14, 1853. Appeal dismissed by the District Court Nov. 26, 1856. Patent issued to Elam Brown May 18, 1858, for 3,328.95 acres.' The catalogue's structured Creator field separates the roles explicitly: 'Valencia, Candelario, 1804-1881, Grantee'; 'Brown, Elam, 1797-1889, Claimant'; 'Brown, Elam, 1797-1889, Patentee'. That is the same split the register makes (grantee Candelario Valencia, patent_to Elam Brown), and Hoffman 1862 agrees on 1834 / Jose Figueroa / Candelario Valencia / confirmed / patented. Three independent secondary sources therefore agree with the register on all four substantive fields, and on the outcome the sequence is Board confirmation 14 Feb. 1853 followed by DISMISSAL of the appeal, not a reversal - so the register's bare 'Confirmed' is very likely sound and is NOT the trap case. None of that is decree evidence, which is why every one of those fields is UV and not OK. The file is only 35.8 MB, the smallest of the three I could not reach, so it is the cheapest to finish first. Bowman also flags a boundary dispute with Joaquin Moraga over the line between Acalanes and Laguna de los Palos Colorados (Deposited Expediente 14, 1843; Interior Dept. decision 23 Feb. 1882), and notes the ranch was also called San Felipe - a possible alias worth carrying in the register.
